newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian finance minister to meet bank chiefs.
newsitem.headline: Indian finance minister to meet bank chiefs.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was set to meet the heads of the country's state-run banks later on Monday to discuss ways to streamline the banking system, a ministry spokeswoman said.
"It will be a very general meeting," she said, adding that the heads of some 27 banks were expected to attend the meeting, set to start in the late afternoon.
"It will not focus on the capital markets but rather on how to streamline the banking sector."
The Financial Express newspaper said commercial banks were under pressure from the Finance Ministry to purchase shares from the secondary market without further delay.

The daily said the ministry was exploring the possibility of lifting a cap on banks' investment in shares and debentures from the existing level of five percent of the incremental deposits of the previous year.

The spokeswoman said the meeting was expected to focus on the credit scenario, the reduction of non-performing assets, the recovery of bad debts and the improvement of internal control systems. Participants were also expected to discuss rural credit and credit to weaker industrial sectors, as well as modernisation and customer service.
